selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveler want to learn when he turned his attention to the World of the Unseen?
questions.answer: He wanted to know what that hidden world would reveal about its Maker.

questions.question: What evidence in the visible world leads him to think there is One who wants to be known?
questions.answer: The abundance of beautifully made works and generous blessings leads him to that conclusion.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveler reach from the fact that the Creator makes Himself known through works and blessings?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Creator must also make Himself known through speech.

questions.question: Why would spoken communication naturally follow this kind of action-based communication?
questions.answer: Because One who intentionally introduces Himself through deeds would also speak to make that introduction clearer.

questions.question: How does the testimony that comes through revelation compare with the testimony of the universe and created things?
questions.answer: It is presented as stronger than the witness given by the universe and its creatures.

questions.question: What central truths are carried by revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: They carry witness to Allah’s existence and His oneness.

questions.question: What makes the reality of revelation almost self-evident in the passage?
questions.answer: The agreement of many prophets, along with the proofs and miracles found in sacred books and pages.

questions.question: What large-scale human evidence supports the certainty of revelation?
questions.answer: The united witness of a huge number of prophets supports it.

questions.question: What additional evidence supports revelation besides the prophets’ agreement?
questions.answer: The miracles and proofs found in the sacred scriptures and revealed pages.

questions.question: What new observation does he make after this about inspiration?
questions.answer: He observes that true inspiration resembles revelation in some respects.

questions.question: At the start of the passage, what question was in the traveler’s mind as he approached the unseen realm?
questions.answer: He was wondering what message that realm had to give.

questions.question: What signs in the visible world point to a Maker who wants a relationship with His creation?
questions.answer: The carefully made works, abundant gifts, and signs of hidden perfection point to that.

questions.question: Through what means does the passage first say these purposes are shown?
questions.answer: Through actions, blessings, and the natural language of created conditions.

questions.question: From what perspective does the traveler seek knowledge of the unseen after this conclusion?
questions.answer: He seeks it through the manifestations that come from that realm.

questions.question: How is the presence of revelation in the unseen world described?
questions.answer: It is described as dominating that world at all times and in every part.

questions.question: What mistaken idea about divine self-disclosure does the passage reject?
questions.answer: It rejects the idea that Allah only lets creation speak for Him without speaking Himself.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s speech in relation to His knowledge and power?
questions.answer: Since He is present everywhere by knowledge and power, His speech is also without end.

questions.question: What historical-religious consensus is used to support revelation?
questions.answer: The united testimony of one hundred thousand prophets is used.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand before moving on to inspiration?
questions.answer: He understood that revelation declares five sacred truths.

questions.question: What does the passage say the traveler understood revelation to announce?
questions.answer: He understood that it proclaims five holy truths.

questions.question: What moved the traveler to “knock” on the unseen world, in a figurative sense?
questions.answer: His desire to discover what that hidden realm says about the One behind creation.

questions.question: What features of the physical world lead him to believe there is One behind the veil of the unseen?
questions.answer: Its beauty, artistry, blessings, and amazing order lead him to that belief.

questions.question: Why does the traveler think spoken communication must also exist?
questions.answer: Because a being who reveals Himself so clearly through actions would not leave that self-disclosure without speech.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from that for the traveler?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Creator certainly also speaks.
